answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation with a slow climb: a new agent starts at the base of an ivory tower of trust, earning small attestations for real work, and only after sustained verified service reaches the summit where its votes carry weight. A sybil swarm can fake many identities, but each clone must repeat the same costly climb, so the attack cost grows linearly while one honest agent's plume of earned history keeps compounding. Identity becomes earned, not claimed.
